items.excerpt: The pan-European STOXX 600 ended 1% lower on Wednesday, giving up most of its gains from the last three sessions, and bank shares fell 3.3%. Oil held near $100 a barrel on renewed Middle East tension, and worries about France's finances pushed the euro down 0.6% to $1.119. Trading Economics put the Euro STOXX 50 down 1.6% at 6,175.

sx5e.mechanism: French and Italian bond yields rose much faster than German yields, so future company profits looked less valuable and banks that hold those bonds were sold, which pulled the Euro Stoxx 50 down 1.47%.
sx5e.outlook: The index stays tied to French and Italian bond yields and to oil near $100 until the ECB meets on 29 Oct.

points.text: A global bond sell-off pushed the US 30-year Treasury yield to a fresh 24-year high, and yields in heavily indebted euro zone countries rose faster than German yields, so future company profits looked less valuable, which made European shares less attractive and pushed the Euro Stoxx 50 down 1.47%.

France's 10-year yield jumped 15 basis points (hundredths of a percent) and Italy's 10, while German yields were flat, because investors doubt France can fix its finances before the 2027 election, so worry about European debt spread, which pushed the Euro Stoxx 50 down.

Rising yields cut the value of the government bonds banks hold, so Deutsche Bank fell 5% and UniCredit, Intesa Sanpaolo and BNP Paribas fell about 4% each, which pulled the Euro Stoxx 50 down 1.47% because banks are a big part of the index.
Oil rose back above $100 a barrel on Middle East tension, so a Milan fund manager said an inflation spike would keep rates high, which added pressure on banks and pushed the Euro Stoxx 50 lower.

Industrial shares also fell, with Siemens and Safran down 3% each and Schneider Electric down 2.3% as investors kept judging its deal to buy PTC, so selling spread beyond banks, which added to the Euro Stoxx 50's 1.47% drop.

nextPoints.text: Expect more weakness while French and Italian yields keep rising faster than German ones, because that hits the banks that carry big weight in the index.
A calmer French bond market or oil falling back below $100 would ease the pressure on banks and let the index recover.
The ECB announces its next rate decision on Thursday 29 Oct, one day after the Fed's decision on 28 Oct.

also.title: Hong Kong Stocks Tumble After China's Golden Week Holiday; Hang Seng Tech Index Hits Two-Year Low as HSBC and Standard Chartered Lead Declines
Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index closes 1.43 pct lower

items.excerpt: The Hang Seng Index dropped 344 points, or 1.4%, to 23,785 on Thursday, its lowest level in three months, on turnover of HK$207.26 billion. The tech index fell 2.9% to 4,073, its lowest in two years. Mainland traders returning from the week-long holiday faced renewed geopolitical tension and higher global yields, and the CSI300 fell 1.1% to a one-year low.

hsi.mechanism: High US long-term yields, a near 5% drop in HSBC and Standard Chartered, and a chip sell-off after Samsung's results pulled money out of Hong Kong, which pushed the Hang Seng down 1.43%.
hsi.outlook: Hong Kong stays near three-month lows while US long-term yields stay above 5%.

points.text: The US 10-year yield touched 5.34% during China's holiday, so brokerage China Securities said fast-rising 30-year US yields would draw money out of China, which pushed the Hang Seng down 1.43%.

High long-term bond yields and talk of UK tax rises on banks hit HSBC and Standard Chartered, so HSBC fell nearly 5% and Standard Chartered 5.5%, which together cut more than 100 points from the Hang Seng and pushed it down 1.43%.

Samsung Electronics reported a record 107.4 trillion won quarterly operating profit but still missed high hopes, so chip shares such as Hua Hong Semiconductor fell more than 9% in Hong Kong, which added to the Hang Seng's 1.43% drop.

Mainland markets and Stock Connect reopened after Golden Week, but the CSI300 fell to a one-year low, so returning mainland money did not buy Hong Kong shares, which left the Hang Seng without support and it fell 1.43%.

The US Federal Communications Commission said it would vote on 29 Oct to bar all Chinese labs from testing electronics for the US market, so US-China tension rose again, which added selling pressure on the Hang Seng.

nextPoints.text: Hong Kong stays weak near three-month lows while US long-term yields stay above 5%, because high yields pull money away from Chinese tech shares.
A drop in US Treasury yields or new Chinese stimulus steps could bring buyers back to the beaten-down tech index.
China's September consumer price data comes out on Wednesday 14 Oct.

hsi.mechanism: Trump's pledge not to attack Iran before the midterms eased oil-spike fears, and internet and financial shares bounced from Thursday's low, which pushed the Hang Seng up 1.79%.
hsi.outlook: The rebound is fragile because the tech index is still near a two-year low and US yields remain high.

points.text: US President Donald Trump said the US would not attack Iran before November's midterm elections, so fears of an oil spike eased, which pushed the Hang Seng up 0.65% at the open and helped it close 1.79% higher.
Internet companies led the rebound, with Xiaomi up nearly 10% and Alibaba, Meituan and Tencent up about 3% or more, so the tech index rose 3.1%, which pushed the Hang Seng up 1.79%.

Heavyweight financial shares also rose, with Hong Kong Exchanges, HSBC and AIA up between about 1% and 3% a day after HSBC's near 5% drop, so the biggest names in the index bounced, which added to the Hang Seng's 1.79% gain.

Wall Street tech shares fell overnight on a report that OpenAI's yearly revenue was $20 billion less than signalled, and mainland AI supply-chain shares kept falling, so Hong Kong rose on its own rebound rather than a Wall Street lift, which still left the Hang Seng up 1.79%.

nextPoints.text: Hong Kong can hold above 24,000 if internet shares keep recovering, but the tech index near a two-year low leaves little room for bad news.
A US move against Iran that sends oil higher, or a new jump in US Treasury yields, could undo Friday's gain.
China's September consumer price data comes out on Wednesday 14 Oct.

Big banks including JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs and Wells Fargo report next week, and analysts expect S&P 500 third-quarter earnings growth of 30.6%.

spx.mechanism: Monday's 0.66%, Tuesday's 0.58% and Friday's 0.59% gains did most of the 1.14% weekly rise, led by AI shares such as Nvidia, so a 24-year high in yields on Wednesday and an OpenAI revenue report on Thursday caused the two down days, which still left the S&P 500 up 1.14% for the week.

points.text: Monday's AI-led session, with Nvidia up 2.12% to a record close, so six AI leaders added about 0.44 percentage points on their own, which pushed the S&P 500 up 0.66% that day.

Tuesday's 0.58% rise gave the S&P 500 a record close, so Monday, Tuesday and Friday did most of the week's work and big AI shares were the common thread, which pushed the S&P 500 up 1.14% for the week.
Treasury yields hit a 24-year high on Wednesday, so future company profits looked less valuable, which pushed the S&P 500 down 0.22% that day, with the 10-year still about 5.23% on Thursday.

The Financial Times reported OpenAI's yearly revenue was near $50 billion, about $20 billion below earlier reports, so chip companies that sell to OpenAI were sold, which sent the chip index down 3.39% and pushed the S&P 500 down 0.47% on Thursday.

President Trump pledged not to attack Iran before the midterm elections, so oil-spike fears eased, which pushed the S&P 500 up 0.59% on Friday, though a Baird analyst called it a fairly tepid rally because Iran headlines keep changing.

nextPoints.text: A slow upward lean while yields stay below Wednesday's high, because analysts expect S&P 500 profits to have grown 30.6% in the third quarter.
A hot September CPI reading would revive Fed rate-hike bets and push yields back toward their highs, which would hit expensive tech shares first.
JPMorgan reports on Tuesday 13 Oct, September CPI comes out on Wednesday 14 Oct, and the Fed decides on Wednesday 28 Oct.

items.excerpt: Reports that Spain's government was preparing an early election pushed EUR/USD to its lowest since May 2025, and hedge-fund selling in Asia set off option barriers that deepened the fall. The pair later recovered more than half of that drop and traded back above 1.1200 after Prime Minister Sánchez confirmed a 29 November vote. ECB Chief Economist Lane said costlier energy and higher long-term borrowing costs are already slowing demand, which could limit how far the ECB has to raise rates from its 2.50% deposit rate.

eur.mechanism: Investors kept selling French government bonds after France's 2027 budget, and reports of a snap Spanish election added a second political worry, so EUR/USD dropped to a 17-month low near 1.1150 in Asia, then recovered more than half of that and closed down 0.28% at 1.1221.
eur.outlook: EUR/USD leans lower while the gap between French and German bond yields stays wide, with the Fed minutes and the ECB account as the next tests.

points.text: Oxford Economics' Ricardo Amaro said bets on higher Fed rates as global bond yields rise kept the dollar strong, so holding euros paid less than holding dollars, which left EUR/USD down about 5% in 2026 and set up Monday's extra drop.

France's 10-year bond yield had climbed to 5% last week and its gap over German yields reached the widest since the euro debt crisis, so investors sold euros along with French bonds, which pushed EUR/USD to its lowest since May 2025.

Reports that Spain was heading for an early election set off hedge-fund selling in Asia that tripped option barriers (preset price levels that trigger more selling), so more selling followed automatically, which pushed EUR/USD to just above 1.1150.

ECB Chief Economist Philip Lane said higher energy costs and borrowing costs are already slowing demand, so traders saw a chance of fewer ECB hikes than the two to three priced, which took away some rate support and added to the euro's drop.

Prime Minister Sánchez's confirmation of a 29 November vote did less damage than the earlier reports, so some of the forced selling reversed, which pulled EUR/USD back above 1.1200 and shrank the daily loss to 0.28%.

nextPoints.text: EUR/USD leans lower while it stays below 1.1300, because French and Spanish politics add risk at the same time as the ECB may hike less.
A narrower gap between French and German yields or Fed minutes that show less appetite for hikes would give the euro room to bounce.
Wednesday 7 October at 18:00 GMT the Fed releases its September minutes, and Thursday 8 October at 11:30 GMT the ECB publishes the account of its September meeting.

gbp.outlook: GBP/USD is back near the top of its range, and the Fed minutes decide whether it breaks higher or falls back toward 1.3200.

points.text: US Treasury yields came off Monday's 24-year high, so holding dollars paid a little less, which pushed GBP/USD up 0.40% to 1.3272.

The US dollar index fell 0.31% to 101.78 and the US trade deficit widened in August as imports hit a record, so the dollar lost ground against all the big currencies, which pushed GBP/USD higher with them.

nextPoints.text: GBP/USD can hold near the top of its 1.3200 to 1.3300 range while US yields stay off their highs.

Wednesday 7 October at 18:00 GMT: minutes of the Fed's 16 September meeting, where it raised rates to 3.75%-4.00%.

items.title: Euro falls 0.6% as French bond stress returns and Fed minutes point to another hike

items.excerpt: The US dollar index gained 0.4% to 102.24, near its strongest level since 9 April 2025, after minutes from the Fed's September meeting showed most officials thought another rate increase would likely be appropriate by the end of 2026. eur.mechanism: US long-term yields climbed and the Fed minutes backed another hike this year, which lifted the dollar, while selling of French bonds started again, so the euro became the weakest major currency and EUR/USD fell 0.56% to 1.1195.
eur.outlook: EUR/USD leans lower while the French-German yield gap stays above about 140 basis points and the Fed keeps a hike on the table.

points.text: The US 10-year yield rose 5.9 basis points (hundredths of a percent) to 5.345% as Brent held above $100, so dollar deposits paid more than euro deposits, which pulled money out of the euro and pushed EUR/USD down.
Minutes of the Fed's September meeting showed most officials expected another rate rise by the end of 2026, so the dollar index rose 0.4% to 102.24, which pushed EUR/USD down 0.56% to 1.1195.

The gap between French and German 10-year yields widened to 141.2 basis points from 129.7 at Tuesday's close, so Tuesday's relief lasted one day and investors sold euros again, which made the euro the weakest major currency and added to the 0.56% fall.

IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva told France to "get your house in order" because its deficit is 5.4% of GDP and its budget plan only aims for 5% next year, so investors kept selling French bonds, which pushed the euro lower with them.

nextPoints.text: EUR/USD leans lower while French yields keep rising faster than US yields.
A fall in the French-German yield gap back toward 130 basis points, or a soft US inflation report that cuts Fed hike bets, would let the euro recover.
Thursday 8 October: the ECB publishes the account of its September meeting, then Wednesday 14 October brings US September CPI.

items.excerpt: President Trump said on Thursday that the US would not resume military strikes on Iran before the 3 November midterm elections and that talks with Iran were productive, which kept a lid on oil prices and eased worries about inflation. A well-received 30-year bond auction also pulled US yields lower, and USD/CHF slid from near the mid-0.8300s, a one-week high. Traders still price an over-80% chance of another Fed hike by year-end, against the Swiss National Bank's wait-and-see stance.

chf.mechanism: USD/CHF rose in the morning after the SNB ruled out near-term hikes, then Trump promised no Iran strike before the midterms and a strong 30-year auction pulled US yields down, so the dollar was sold across the board, which pushed USD/CHF down 0.20% to 0.8314.
chf.outlook: USD/CHF may drift lower while US yields stay off their highs, but the gap between Fed and SNB rates limits how far it can fall.

points.text: The US 10-year yield ended near 5.22% after touching its highest since 2002 on Wednesday, so the dollar lost some of its yield advantage over the franc, which pushed USD/CHF down 0.20% to 0.8314.

President Trump posted that the US would not attack Iran before the 3 November midterms, and US crude fell from about $92.70 to $90.50 within minutes, so inflation fears and the case for more Fed hikes eased, which took buying out of the dollar and pushed USD/CHF lower.

A well-received 30-year Treasury auction showed strong demand for US bonds, so yields fell further and traders took profits on the dollar's rally to its highest since April 2025, which pushed USD/CHF down.

Earlier in the day SNB Vice Chairman Antoine Martin said Switzerland remains "comfortably within" its 0% to 2% price goal, so near-term Swiss rate hikes were ruled out, which first pushed USD/CHF up to near 0.8350 before the US news reversed it and left the pair down 0.20%.

nextPoints.text: USD/CHF can drift lower while US yields stay below their highs, but the Fed's hike plans against the SNB's 0% rate should stop a deep fall.
A hot US inflation report or new trouble in US-Iran talks would push US yields and USD/CHF back up toward the 17-month high near 0.8380.
Wednesday 14 October: US consumer price inflation (CPI) for September.

Money markets put an 81% chance on the Fed holding rates in October and an 81% chance of a December hike.

aud.mechanism: US yields stayed below the week's high after Thursday's drop and US consumer confidence came in weak, so the dollar gave back some of its gains and investors bought stocks, which pushed AUD/USD up 0.39% to 0.6982.
aud.outlook: AUD/USD may hold near 0.70, but it stays below its 20-day average and needs strong Australian jobs data or soft US inflation to climb further.

points.text: Danske Bank noted a solid drop in US yields on Thursday after a strong 30-year Treasury auction, so the dollar became less attractive to hold, which helped push AUD/USD up 0.39% to 0.6982.
The University of Michigan consumer sentiment index fell to 46.3 from 48.1, below the 47.6 forecast, so bets on a Fed hold on 28 October rose, which weighed on the dollar and pushed AUD/USD higher.

S&P 500 futures rose 0.33% to near 7,800 as investors bought shares, so the Aussie, a currency that tends to move with stocks, rose with them, which made it the strongest major currency and pushed AUD/USD up 0.39%.

The same survey showed 1-year inflation expectations rising to 4.7% and 5-year to 3.5%, and Fed officials Waller and Musalem argued for more hikes, so an 81% chance of a December hike stayed priced, which limited how far the dollar fell and capped the Aussie's gain.

nextPoints.text: AUD/USD may hold near 0.6980 but stays capped below its 20-day average near 0.7020 while US yields remain above 5.2%.
A strong Australian jobs report or RBA minutes that keep another hike in play would lift the Aussie, while hot US inflation would push it back down.
Tuesday 13 October RBA minutes, Wednesday 14 October US September CPI, and Thursday 15 October Australia's September jobs report.

also.title: Week Ahead – US CPI, France's Budget Crisis and Q3 Earnings to Set the Market Tone
Weekly Focus – French Public Finances Continue to Steal the Spotlight

items.excerpt: EUR/USD reversed earlier gains on Friday and stayed on track for a fifth consecutive weekly decline as the US dollar rebounded and the 10-year Treasury yield rose 4.2 basis points to 5.261%, below the week's 5.365% peak, its highest since 2002. ING warned that the "French premium isn't likely to leave the euro very soon" and that "risks remain of a test of 1.110 in the near term".

eur.mechanism: Wednesday (−0.56%) and Monday (−0.28%) did most of the week's 0.45% fall, both on French bond selling, and Wednesday also had hawkish Fed minutes, so French debt risk sat on top of US yields near their highest since 2002, which left EUR/USD down 0.45% for the week.
eur.outlook: EUR/USD leans lower while France's budget fight goes on and markets cut ECB hike bets, with US CPI on 14 October as the next big test.

points.text: On Wednesday the gap between French and German 10-year yields jumped back to 141.2 basis points and the Fed minutes lifted the dollar to a nearly 18-month high, so investors sold euros on both counts, which pushed EUR/USD down 0.56% that day, the week's biggest drop.

On Monday, reports of a snap Spanish election and more selling of French bonds hit at the same time, so investors sold euros along with those bonds, which pushed EUR/USD to its lowest since May 2025, near 1.1150, before it recovered to close down 0.28%.

The euro's gains on Tuesday (+0.33%) and Thursday (+0.13%) came only when US yields dipped, and on Friday the 10-year rose 4.2 basis points to 5.261%, so dollar deposits paid more again, which pulled EUR/USD down 0.07% to 1.1201 and left it 0.45% lower on the week.

Euro zone money markets cut expected ECB hikes to 70 basis points by the end of 2027 from 100 a few days earlier, and Danske Bank said the French turmoil makes an October ECB hike unlikely, so the euro lost rate support, which added to the week's 0.45% fall.

nextPoints.text: EUR/USD leans lower, and ING sees a risk of a test of 1.1100 soon because the French risk premium is not likely to fade quickly.
A softer-than-expected US CPI report or real progress on France's 2027 budget, whose detailed debate starts in the National Assembly on Tuesday 13 October, could give the euro a lift.
Wednesday 14 October US September CPI, then the Fed decision on 28 October and the ECB meeting on 29 October.

items.title: Oil falls as G7 reserve release and higher Gulf exports add supply

also.title: CRUDE WRAP: WTI (X6) settles USD 1.68 lower at 89.43/bbl

items.excerpt: US West Texas Intermediate crude lost $1.68, or 1.84%, to settle at $89.43 on Monday, and Brent fell $1.93 to $100.32. Middle Eastern crude exports rose above pre-war levels on four of the seven days in the last week of September, and G7 countries agreed on Friday to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude from emergency reserves. US Strategic Petroleum Reserve stocks fell to 283 million barrels, the lowest since October 1982.

wti.mechanism: G7 countries agreed to release 100 million barrels from emergency stocks and Middle East exports recovered above pre-war levels, so more oil was headed to buyers, which pushed WTI down 1.84% to $89.43. Reports of Houthi strikes on Saudi refineries raised fears of lost barrels, which kept WTI from falling further.
wti.outlook: More barrels reaching buyers leans prices lower. A hit to Saudi export facilities or new trouble at Hormuz would reverse that.

points.text: G7 countries agreed on Friday to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude from emergency reserves, so extra oil was headed to the market, which pushed WTI down $1.68, or 1.84%, to $89.43 on Monday.

Shipping data showed Middle Eastern crude exports above pre-war levels on four of the seven days in the last week of September, even with attacks on tankers near the Strait of Hormuz, so traders expected more oil to reach buyers, which pushed WTI down.

Raymond James analyst Pavel Molchanov said traders doubted how much of the G7 oil was new, because it may come from the 400 million barrels already pledged in March, so the extra supply looked smaller than advertised, which limited how far WTI fell.

Reports of a Houthi missile strike on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery and an explosion at a Jeddah refinery raised fears of lost Saudi barrels, so buyers briefly paid more, which pushed WTI as high as $91.88 before it closed lower after swinging from $88.88.

nextPoints.text: Lean lower for the next few sessions, because emergency stocks and recovering Gulf exports are adding barrels.
A successful attack on Saudi export facilities or new tanker damage near Hormuz would push prices back up.
The EIA weekly US petroleum inventory report on Wednesday 7 October.

items.title: Wheat climbs above $7 on a weaker dollar and Black Sea ship attacks

also.title: EU wheat holds firm as Black Sea attacks continue
Grains Bounce on Corrective Buying, Harvest, War Premium

items.excerpt: December Chicago wheat climbed 12 cents to $7.04¼ on Tuesday, and December Kansas City wheat added 14 cents to $7.56¼. Short-covering and a weaker dollar helped the rally, while escalating Russia-Ukraine tensions renewed concern about Black Sea grain shipments. Reuters reported two merchant ships, one carrying grain, were hit by a drone strike in the Black Sea off Bulgaria the same day.

wh.mechanism: The US dollar eased and funds bought back short bets after last week's 15-to-25-cent drop, so American wheat looked cheaper to foreign buyers and shorts had to buy, which pushed December wheat up 12 cents to $7.04¼. Two drone attacks on Black Sea ships raised fears that less grain would ship, which added to the rise in wheat.
wh.outlook: Analysts see the bounce as fund buying, not a real shortage, so wheat may stall near $7. Friday's USDA report is the next test.

points.text: DePutter said the US dollar eased, so American wheat became cheaper for foreign buyers, which pushed December Chicago wheat up 12 cents to $7.04¼.

Barchart's Darin Newsom said funds bought back short bets (bets on a fall) after wheat lost 15 to 25 cents last week, so extra buying hit the market without any change in supply, which pushed wheat up.

Two merchant ships, one carrying grain, were hit by a drone strike off Bulgaria on Tuesday, a day after Russia sank two vessels carrying Ukrainian corn and wheat, so traders feared less Black Sea grain would ship, which pushed wheat up.

Traders said Russia shipped about 255,000 tons of wheat through Baltic Sea ports last week, up from 175,000 tons, so some Russian wheat still reached buyers on other routes, which limited how far wheat rose.

nextPoints.text: Lean sideways near $7, because Newsom said the basis (cash price minus futures) and futures spreads still show no shortage of wheat.
A strike that knocks out Ukraine's Danube or Odessa export capacity for weeks would give buyers a lasting reason to pay more.
The USDA WASDE supply and demand report on Friday 9 October at noon Eastern time.

items.title: Natural gas jumps as Tropical Storm Isaias threatens Gulf output
items.excerpt: November natural gas futures traded at $3.197, up 8.3 cents or 2.67%, at 11:23 GMT on Wednesday, extending the rebound from last week's $2.912 low. Tropical Storm Isaias was expected to become a hurricane by Thursday and producers were pulling crews off Gulf platforms. Analysts expected Thursday's EIA report to show a 79 Bcf storage build against a five-year average near 96 Bcf.

ng.mechanism: Tropical Storm Isaias put Gulf of Mexico gas output at risk and a light expected storage build made short sellers buy back, so supply looked tighter, which pushed natural gas up 2.86% to about $3.20.
ng.outlook: The storm and Thursday's storage number drive the next few days. Near-record output and warm weather still cap the rally.

points.text: Tropical Storm Isaias was forecast to become a hurricane by Thursday and producers began pulling crews off Gulf platforms, so Gulf gas output was at risk of shutting, which pushed natural gas up 2.86% to about $3.20.

Analysts expected Thursday's EIA report to show a 79 Bcf (billion cubic feet) storage build, well below the five-year average near 96 Bcf, so the supply cushion looked thinner, which pushed natural gas up.

With gas already up from last week's low of $2.912, short sellers (traders betting on a fall) did not want to stay exposed to a storm and bought back, so extra buying hit the market, which pushed natural gas higher.

US output stayed near record, autumn weather was warm across much of the country, and the storm could also cut power demand and LNG export demand, so extra gas supply and weaker demand still loomed, which limited how far natural gas rose.

nextPoints.text: Lean slightly higher while Isaias is in the Gulf, because traders will not bet against gas before they know how much output it shuts.
A storage build well above 79 Bcf, or a storm track that misses production, would take the storm premium out.
The EIA weekly natural gas storage report on Thursday 8 October.

also.title: CRUDE WRAP: WTI (X6) settles USD 3.21 higher at 91.49/bbl

items.excerpt: West Texas Intermediate futures rose 3.6% to settle at $91.49 a barrel on Thursday and Brent gained 4% to $104.28, as Iran stepped up attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Hurricane Isaias threatened US offshore output. Oil companies shut in about 500,000 barrels per day, or 25% of Gulf of Mexico production. Prices came off their highs after President Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the November midterm elections.

wti.mechanism: Reports of US strike plans against Iran, nine tanker attacks near Hormuz in a week and storm shut-ins in the Gulf of Mexico made traders fear less oil would reach buyers, so the supply risk rose, which pushed WTI up 3.6% to $91.49. President Trump promised no attack before the midterms, so the war-risk premium faded, which pulled WTI back from the $93.20 high.
wti.outlook: Tanker attacks and storm shut-ins keep supply risk in the price. Iran's reply to the US reopening proposal is the main swing factor.

points.text: Reports said Washington had finished operational plans for possible strikes on Iran, so a new war could cut more Gulf oil, which pushed WTI up to a session high of $93.20.

Nine tankers were attacked in and around the Strait of Hormuz over the past week, and Kpler data showed flows through the strait about 30% below pre-war levels, so less oil was getting through, which pushed WTI up 3.6% to $91.49.

Oil companies shut in about 500,000 barrels per day, or 25% of Gulf of Mexico offshore output, as Hurricane Isaias headed for Alabama, Mississippi and the Florida panhandle, so US supply fell, which pushed WTI up.
Iran-backed Houthi militants fired missiles at Riyadh and Abha on Tuesday and Wednesday and again on Thursday, so Saudi oil facilities looked more at risk, which pushed WTI up.
President Trump said talks with Iran were productive and the US would not attack before the November midterms, so the war-risk premium faded, which pulled WTI back from its $93.20 high.

nextPoints.text: Lean sideways to higher, because tanker attacks near Hormuz and storm shut-ins in the Gulf of Mexico have not cleared.
Iran accepting the US proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz would remove much of the supply worry and pull prices down.
The EIA weekly US petroleum inventory report, moved to Thursday 15 October at noon Eastern time because of the Columbus Day holiday.

Oil fell and bargain buyers stepped in after Thursday's close below $60, so extra demand hit the metal, which added to Friday's rise in silver.
ag.outlook: Silver bounced, but markets still expect a Fed hike by December. Wednesday's CPI will decide whether yields fall further.

points.text: Thursday's strong 30-year Treasury auction eased pressure on long-term rates and the 10-year yield fell to about 5.24% from about 5.33%, so silver, a metal that pays no interest, became more attractive, which pushed silver up 2.73% to about $61.05.
The dollar softened early in the session, so silver became cheaper for buyers using other currencies, which pushed silver up.
Oil fell after President Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the midterms, so inflation worries eased and yields pulled lower, which pushed silver up.
Silver had closed below $60 on Thursday after the week's rate-driven selloff, so bargain buyers stepped in at that level on Friday, which pushed silver up.

nextPoints.text: Lean slightly higher toward the $61.72 to $63.06 area Kitco flags as resistance, as long as yields stay below this week's highs.
A hot September CPI would raise the 84% chance of a December Fed hike and push yields back up, which would hit silver.
US CPI for September on Wednesday 14 October at 8:30 a.m. Eastern time.

items.title: Natural gas gains about 6% in a week of Hurricane Isaias and falling output

also.title: Week Ending October 9
Natural Gas News: Isaias Has Shorts Covering as November Gas Tests Resistance

items.excerpt: November gas futures rose 5.2 cents on Friday to a two-week high of $3.22 per million Btu as Hurricane Isaias approached the US Gulf Coast and US production fell below its early-October level. A bearish storage report had halted a five-session, 23.6-cent rally on Thursday. Aegis said the EIA's 85 Bcf injection was slightly larger than expected but left storage only 68 Bcf above the five-year average, down from nearly 200 Bcf eight weeks ago.

ng.mechanism: Hurricane Isaias threatened Gulf output while US production fell, so supply looked tighter, which pushed natural gas up 6.10% for the week to about $3.22, with Wednesday (+2.86%), Friday (+1.64%) and Tuesday (+1.57%) doing most of the move. Thursday's EIA storage build came in slightly larger than expected, so the cushion looked a bit thicker, which pushed natural gas down that day.
ng.outlook: Aegis expects offshore output to return quickly after the storm and the storm to cut power demand. Without colder forecasts, the rally may struggle to hold.

points.text: Tropical Storm Isaias formed in the Gulf on Wednesday and short sellers (traders betting on a fall) bought back, so extra buying hit the market, which pushed natural gas up 2.86% that day after a 1.57% gain on Tuesday.

Hurricane Isaias interrupted offshore production on Friday ahead of landfall and US production fell below its early-October level, so fewer gas barrels were coming to market, which pushed natural gas up 5.2 cents, or 1.64%, to a two-week high of $3.22.

The EIA reported an 85 Bcf (billion cubic feet) storage build on Thursday, slightly larger than expected, so the storage cushion looked a bit thicker, which pushed natural gas down 1.09% and ended a five-session, 23.6-cent rally.
Even after that build, storage was only 68 Bcf above the five-year average, down from nearly 200 Bcf eight weeks ago, so the surplus was shrinking, which pushed natural gas up for the week.

nextPoints.text: Lean sideways to lower after the storm passes, because Aegis expects offshore output to recover quickly and hurricanes usually cut power demand.
Colder late-October forecasts or longer storm damage to Gulf production would keep the rally going.
The EIA weekly natural gas storage report on Thursday 15 October.

items.title: Gilt yields rise again as US service firms report the fastest price rises since 2022

also.title: US Treasury yields scale multi-year highs as inflation fears return
End of Day Wrap-Up, 5 October 2026

items.excerpt: In late European trading on Monday 5 October, the UK 10-year gilt yield rose 6.2 basis points to a daily high of 5.428%, close to the 1 October peak of 5.504%. The 2-year gilt yield rose 2.8 basis points to 4.846%, and the 30-year yield rose 5.2 basis points.

gb10y.mechanism: A US survey showed service firms paying the highest prices since 2022, so US long-term yields rose to new highs and gilts were sold along with Treasuries, which pushed the UK 10-year yield up about 6.5 basis points to about 5.42%.
gb10y.outlook: Gilt yields are likely to stay near their highs while the global bond selloff continues and the 28 October budget gets closer. A clear fall in US yields would be the main thing to pull them down.

points.text: The US ISM survey showed the prices paid by service firms jumped to 74.0 in September, the highest since July 2022, so investors feared inflation will keep central banks raising rates, which led them to sell long-dated government bonds and pushed the UK 10-year gilt yield higher.

The US 10-year Treasury yield rose more than 3 basis points to 5.307%, so gilts were sold with Treasuries, which pushed the UK 10-year yield up about 6.5 basis points (hundredths of a percentage point) to about 5.42%.

UK data were not the trigger, because the September services PMI (a survey of service firms) came in at 52.1 against a 51.7 forecast and PWLBtoday said no single UK event explained the move, so the rise in the UK 10-year yield came from the US sell-off, not from home news.

PWLBtoday said worries about government finances in Europe stayed in focus, so investors sold long-dated gilts, which pushed the 30-year gilt yield up 5.2 basis points and added to the 10-year's rise.

nextPoints.text: The 10-year gilt yield is likely to stay near 5.4% to 5.5% in the next few sessions because the global bond selloff has not ended.
A sharp fall in oil prices or in US Treasury yields would ease inflation fears and pull gilt yields down.
Wednesday 28 October: Chancellor John Healey presents his first budget.

items.title: Canadian yields fall as cheaper oil eases inflation fears

also.title: Canadian dollar strengthens, benchmark yield slips

items.excerpt: Canadian government bond yields fell on Tuesday, tracking a broader retreat in global yields as easing oil prices reduced some pressure on inflation expectations. The 10-year yield fell 3.2 basis points to 3.920% and the two-year fell 1.8 basis points to 3.235%, while Brent crude was near $98.48 a barrel.

ca10y.mechanism: Oil fell nearly 2% as Middle East exports recovered and the G7 planned to release emergency fuel stocks, so inflation fears eased, US yields fell and Canadian yields followed, which pushed the Canada 10-year yield down about 4 basis points to about 3.92%.
ca10y.outlook: Canadian yields are likely to keep following oil and US Treasuries. A new jump in oil would push them back up.

points.text: Oil fell nearly 2%, with Brent near $98.48 a barrel, as Middle East exports recovered and the G7 planned to release emergency fuel reserves, so inflation fears eased, which drew buyers to Canadian bonds and pushed the Canada 10-year yield down.

US Treasury yields also fell on Tuesday as oil retreated, so Canadian yields followed them, which pushed the Canada 10-year yield down about 4 basis points (hundredths of a percentage point) to about 3.92%.

The 2-year yield, which tracks expectations for Bank of Canada rates, fell less, by 1.8 basis points to 3.235%, so the 10-year yield was still about 68.5 basis points above it, which shows the drop was a bond-market move, not a bet on an immediate Bank of Canada cut.

Canada's August trade surplus widened to C$4.2 billion, well above forecasts, but the jump came from exports rushed to the US before new tariffs, so it did not change the inflation story, which left the Canada 10-year yield falling with oil and Treasuries.

nextPoints.text: The 10-year yield is likely to stay just below 4% in the next few sessions because it is tracking oil and US Treasuries, which both eased.
A new jump in oil prices on Middle East supply worries would revive inflation fears and push Canadian yields back up.
Friday 9 October: Statistics Canada publishes the September jobs report.

items.title: Gilts sold off as oil tops $100 and UK 30-year yields hit a 1998 high

also.title: UK sells GBP 1.0bln 0.25% 2031 Gilt via tender, b/c 4.39x

items.excerpt: British 30-year gilt yields jumped 13 basis points to peak at 6.036% on Wednesday, their highest since January 1998, as a global bond selloff pushed US 30-year borrowing costs to their highest since 2002. Oil rose further above $100 a barrel, and the 10-year gilt yield rose 10 basis points to 5.48% during the day, just short of its highest since 2007.

gb10y.mechanism: Oil rose above $100 a barrel and a global bond sell-off hit Treasuries and gilts, and worries about extra borrowing in the 28 October budget added to selling, which pushed the UK 10-year yield up about 7.4 basis points to about 5.45%.
gb10y.outlook: Gilt yields are likely to stay near 19-year highs until the budget shows how much the government will borrow. A fall in oil would ease the pressure.

points.text: Oil prices rose further above $100 a barrel because of the US-Israeli war with Iran, so inflation fears rose, which led investors to sell gilts and pushed the UK 10-year yield higher.

The global bond sell-off pushed the US 30-year yield to its highest since 2002 and lifted the US 10-year yield 6 basis points, so gilts were sold harder than Treasuries, which pushed the UK 10-year yield up about 7.4 basis points (hundredths of a percentage point) to about 5.45% at the close.

Bank of America economists forecast that Chancellor John Healey's 28 October budget would add £15 billion to borrowing in both this financial year and 2027/28, so investors worried about more gilt supply, which added selling and pushed the UK 10-year yield up.

The Debt Management Office's sale of £1 billion of 2031 gilts drew bids worth 4.39 times the amount offered, so demand for shorter gilts held up while the heaviest selling hit 30-year bonds, which rose 13 basis points to 6.036% and kept the 10-year yield up 7.4 basis points on the day.

nextPoints.text: The 10-year gilt yield is likely to stay near 5.4% to 5.5% in the next few sessions because investors want to see the budget numbers before buying.
A drop in oil back below $100 a barrel, or a budget plan that cuts borrowing, would bring gilt yields down.
Wednesday 28 October: Chancellor John Healey presents his first budget.

items.title: Strong 30-year Treasury auction pulls long-term yields down from a 2002 high

30-Year Bond Auction, 8 Oct 2026: Results

items.excerpt: US Treasuries rose on Thursday after a 30-year bond auction met solid demand, with the issue pricing at 5.618%, below the expected rate at the bid deadline, and a bid-to-cover ratio of 2.54. The 30-year yield fell 5.9 basis points to 5.602% and the 10-year fell 5 basis points to 5.227% in afternoon trading.

us30y.mechanism: The 30-year yield first rose to its highest since 2002 as oil jumped, then a $22 billion 30-year auction found strong demand, especially from foreign buyers, so investors bought without demanding extra yield, which pushed the US 30-year yield down about 5.5 basis points to about 5.6%.
us30y.outlook: Long-term yields may hold below this week's highs because two big auctions found buyers at these levels. A hot September inflation report would push them back up.

points.text: Oil rose as much as $5 a barrel in the morning on Middle East supply worries, so inflation fears rose, which first pushed the US 30-year yield to 5.732%, its highest since June 2002, before the auction.

The Treasury sold $22 billion of 30-year bonds at 5.618%, below the yield expected at the deadline, with bids worth 2.54 times the amount offered, so investors bought without demanding extra yield, which pushed the US 30-year yield down about 5.5 basis points (hundredths of a percentage point) to about 5.6%.

Indirect bidders, a group that includes foreign central banks and investors, took 72.3% of the 30-year sale against a six-auction average of 69.1%, so foreign money is willing to buy at these yields, which added to the drop in the US 30-year yield.

Oil pulled back slightly after President Trump said the US will not attack Iran before the November midterm elections, so some inflation pressure came off, which helped long-dated bonds and added to the fall in the US 30-year yield.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller said more rate hikes will likely be needed but there is flexibility on the pace, so 2-year yields rose while long yields fell more than short ones, which left the US 30-year yield down about 5.5 basis points on the day.

nextPoints.text: The 30-year yield may hold below Thursday's 5.73% high in the next few sessions because the 10-year and 30-year auctions both found strong demand at these levels.
A hotter-than-expected September inflation report, or another jump in oil, would revive bets on more Fed hikes and push long yields back up.
Wednesday 14 October: the Bureau of Labor Statistics releases the September consumer price index.

items.excerpt: Japanese government bond yields fell for a second session on Friday, with the 10-year yield down 4.5 basis points to 3.035%, its lowest close since September 18, and the 30-year down 5.5 basis points to 4.065%. US Treasury yields retreated after strong demand at a 30-year auction, Japan's own 30-year auction on Thursday saw solid demand, and investors priced the next Bank of Japan hike for December rather than October.

jp10y.mechanism: US Treasury yields fell after a strong 30-year auction, and Japan's own 30-year sale also found buyers, so with traders now expecting the next Bank of Japan hike in December the 10-year JGB yield fell about 7.5 basis points to about 3.01%.
jp10y.outlook: The 10-year JGB yield may hold near 3% because traders no longer expect a Bank of Japan hike in October. A hawkish signal from the bank or new unfunded spending would push it back up.

points.text: US Treasury yields fell overnight after strong demand at a $22 billion 30-year auction, so JGB yields followed across the curve, which pushed the Japan 10-year yield down about 7.5 basis points (hundredths of a percentage point) to about 3.01% at the close.

Japan's 30-year auction on Thursday drew ¥1,747.2 billion of bids for ¥450.7 billion of bonds, about 3.88 times the amount sold, so buyers will take long JGBs at these yields, which added demand and helped push the 10-year yield down.

Investors moved bets for the next Bank of Japan rate hike to December rather than October, after the bank raised its rate to 1.25% in September and signalled a cautious approach, so fewer near-term hikes were priced, which pulled the Japan 10-year yield down.

Cooling expectations for more Fed rate hikes also pushed down both US and Japanese bond yields, so long Japanese bonds were bought with Treasuries, which pushed the 30-year JGB yield down 5.5 basis points to 4.065% and the 10-year down with it.

nextPoints.text: The 10-year JGB yield may hold near 3% in the next few sessions because traders now expect the next Bank of Japan hike in December, not October.
A hint from the Bank of Japan that it could hike in October, or new spending plans without funding, would push the yield back above 3.1%.

jp10y.mechanism: The 10-year JGB yield fell about 8 basis points over the week to about 3.01%, almost all of it on Thursday and Friday, so the common thread was traders pushing the next Bank of Japan hike to December plus strong demand at 30-year auctions in Tokyo and New York, which left the Japan 10-year yield down 2.7% of its level.
jp10y.outlook: The yield may stay near 3% while traders expect the Bank of Japan to wait until December. New spending without funding is the main risk.

points.text: On Monday PM Sanae Takaichi promised to control bond issuance and respond quickly to market turbulence, after the 30-year JGB yield hit a record 4.235% that day, so some of the panic selling stopped, which pushed the Japan 10-year yield down about 1 basis point (hundredth of a percentage point).

On Thursday traders moved bets for the next Bank of Japan hike toward December, so fewer near-term hikes were priced, which pushed the Japan 10-year yield down about 2 basis points, with the Economic Times reporting a 2.5 basis point drop to 3.080% during the day.

Japan's 30-year auction on Thursday drew about 3.88 times the bonds on offer, firmer than the recent average, so buyers were willing to step in at these yields, which added demand and helped push the 10-year yield down.

On Friday US Treasuries rallied after a strong 30-year auction, so Japanese bonds were bought with them, which pushed the Japan 10-year yield down about 7.5 basis points, the biggest move of the week, to end at about 3.01%.

items.excerpt: Solana traded at $120.20 on Monday after four straight daily gains, about 4% below the $124.62 to $125 zone that stopped its last rally. U.S. spot Solana ETFs took in $2.43 million in the week to Oct. 2, down 98.7% from a record $188.22 million the week before. The ISM services prices-paid index rose to 74.0, the highest since July 2022.

sol.mechanism: A stronger dollar and a jump in US service-sector prices pushed short-term yields up, and bitcoin turned back below $87,000 again, so SOL had no fresh ETF buying to lean on, which pushed SOL down 1.83%.
sol.outlook: SOL likely ranges between $114 and $125 until ETF demand returns or Solana confirms a date for its Alpenglow upgrade.

points.text: The US dollar index reached about 102.5 on Monday, its highest in nearly 18 months, as the euro fell toward $1.12, so a stronger dollar makes it harder for assets priced in dollars to attract buyers, which pushed SOL down 1.83%.

The ISM survey showed prices paid by US service firms rising to 74.0, the highest since July 2022, so short-term Treasury yields rose and talk of more Fed rate hikes stayed alive, which made a coin that pays no interest less attractive and pushed SOL down.
Bitcoin came within about $500 of its eight-month high near $87,400 and then fell back under $86,000, so SOL lost the lift it had been getting from the wider market, which added to SOL's 1.83% drop.

US spot Solana ETFs (funds that hold SOL for stock-market investors) took in just $2.43 million in the week to 2 Oct, down 98.7% from a record $188.22 million, so a steady buyer had almost disappeared, which left SOL with less support and it fell 1.83%.

SOL slipped after four straight daily gains and stayed about 4% below the $124.62 to $125 level where sellers stopped the September rally, so there was no fresh news to break that ceiling, which left SOL down 1.83% on the day.

nextPoints.text: SOL likely keeps trading between about $114 and $125, because TradingNEWS sees no fresh ETF demand or confirmed Alpenglow date to push it higher.
A daily close above $125 would open the way to $135, while a stronger dollar and higher yields could push SOL back toward $114.

sol.mechanism: Bond yields, the dollar and oil eased and US stocks hit records, so crypto climbed back from Monday's lows, and SOL also had its own good news in a JPMorgan-advised settlement program, which pushed SOL up 0.98%.
sol.outlook: SOL likely holds near $120 to $122 while bitcoin stays stuck below $87,000. A bitcoin drop under $84,000 is the main risk.

The S&P 500 rose 0.6% to its first record close in two months and the Nasdaq also closed at a record, so crypto climbed from its late-Monday lows and bitcoin touched $86,400, which pulled SOL higher with them.

The Solana Foundation launched Solana DvP, a free open-source program that swaps the asset and the cash in one step within seconds, instead of the one to two days banks usually need, so large institutions have a reason to use the network, which added buying interest and pushed SOL up.

JPMorgan helped shape the program's rules on deadlines and escrow, and the foundation says it passed outside security audits and is ready for real money, so the program looks more credible to regulated firms, which added to SOL's 0.98% gain.

items.excerpt: Bitcoin fell from near $86,600 on Tuesday to as low as about $83,840 early Wednesday as Iran stepped up attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, pushing Brent up almost 1% to about $101.50 and the 10-year Treasury yield up three basis points to 5.31%. DOGE led the losses among the major coins, sliding 5% to about 9 cents.

doge.mechanism: Iran's tanker attacks pushed oil, Treasury yields and the dollar up, and bitcoin broke below $84,000, so borrowed bets on a rise were forced shut and DOGE, the most speculative large coin, fell the most, which pushed DOGE down 6.84%.
doge.outlook: DOGE likely stays weak while oil holds above $100 and yields sit near 2002 highs. Bitcoin below $83,000 would put $80,000 in play.

points.text: Iran stepped up its attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude rose to about $101.50 a barrel, so traders expected higher inflation and higher US yields, which made a coin that pays no interest less attractive and pushed DOGE down 6.84%.

The 10-year Treasury yield climbed three basis points (hundredths of a percent) to 5.31% and the dollar rose against every other G10 currency, so coins that pay no interest looked worse next to bonds, which pushed DOGE down.

Bitcoin dropped from about $86,600 to as low as $83,840, below the $84,000 line FxPro called "a victory for the bears", so DOGE, which usually follows bitcoin but moves more, was already down 5% to about 9 cents by the Asian morning, which left it on the way to a 6.84% daily loss.

Forced closures of borrowed bets (liquidations) jumped 235% to $547 million in 24 hours, according to CoinGlass, so that selling hit the most speculative coins hardest and CoinDesk's Memecoin Index fell about 5%, which added to DOGE's 6.84% drop.
Santiment data show wallets holding 1 million to 100 million DOGE cut their balances by 100 million coins from Tuesday onward, so large holders were selling into the drop, which pushed DOGE lower.

nextPoints.text: DOGE likely stays under pressure for a few sessions, because oil above $100 keeps Treasury yields near their highest since 2002.
Bitcoin breaking below $83,000 would open a quick path to $80,000, according to FxPro, and drag DOGE lower, while Brent falling back under $100 would ease the pressure.

items.excerpt: Solana fell below 110 USDT on Oct. 8, reaching 109.95 USDT as the token posted a 5.46% decline for the day, while a separate quote showed it at $109.22, down 5.93%. Ether also fell below 2,500 USDT in the same market updates.

sol.mechanism: Fed minutes pointed to another rate hike and a report on US strike plans against Iran pushed oil and yields up, so late in the Hong Kong day a wave of forced selling took bitcoin toward $80,400, which pushed SOL down 7.07% and below $110.
sol.outlook: SOL likely stays weak while bitcoin trades below $83,000. Oil falling back under $100 would be the first relief.

points.text: Minutes of the Fed's September meeting, released late Wednesday US time, showed most officials expected another rate hike before year-end, so coins that pay no interest looked less attractive, which pushed SOL down.

A report that the White House asked the Pentagon for strike options against Iran pushed Brent 2% higher to above $102 a barrel and the 10-year Treasury yield up two basis points (hundredths of a percent) to 5.31%, so inflation and rate fears rose again, which added selling and pushed SOL lower.

Bitcoin broke below $83,000, the level FxPro said would confirm sellers were in control, so SOL followed it down and was already down more than 2% by Thursday's Asian morning, which set up the rest of the 7.07% daily loss.

$1.19 billion of crypto bets were forcibly closed in 24 hours, more than $1 billion of them longs (bets on a rise), as bitcoin slid from about $83,200 toward $80,400 late in the day, so forced selling piled on, which pushed SOL below $110.

SOL broke below 110 USDT, down 5.46% at that point, so the $114.42 level that had held earlier in the week was gone, which left SOL on its way to a 7.07% daily loss, the worst of the large coins that day.

nextPoints.text: SOL likely stays weak while bitcoin trades below $83,000, because FxPro sees a quick path to $80,000 from there.
Brent dropping back below $100, where it traded on Tuesday, would take pressure off yields and could let SOL steady.

items.excerpt: XRP rebounded above $1.40 on Friday from weekly lows around $1.32, after a sell-off from weekly highs of $1.53. U.S.-listed spot XRP ETFs recorded $8 million in inflows on Thursday, while perpetual futures open interest dropped to 2.3 billion XRP from 2.4 billion the day before.

xrp.mechanism: Trump's pledge not to strike Iran before the midterms eased oil and calmed markets, and traders who had bet on further falls were forced to buy back, so XRP rose a little more than bitcoin because its ETFs were the only crypto funds still taking in money, which pushed XRP up 2.67%.
xrp.outlook: XRP likely trades around $1.38 to $1.40 until next week's CPI report. A daily close above $1.40 is needed for the bounce to hold.

points.text: President Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the 3 Nov midterm elections, and Brent slipped about 1% to around $103, so oil-driven selling cooled and bitcoin recovered to about $82,500 from Thursday's low near $80,300, which pulled XRP higher with it.

About 78% of the roughly $25 million of crypto bets liquidated in the four hours after Trump's post were short bets (bets on a fall), so those traders were forced to buy back, which added to the bounce and pushed XRP up.

US spot XRP ETFs took in $8 million on Thursday while bitcoin, ether and zcash funds lost money, so XRP had a steady buyer that other coins lacked, which pushed XRP up 2.67%, a little more than bitcoin.

XRP futures open interest (the value of open bets) fell to 2.3 billion XRP from 2.4 billion, so the rise came from spot buying and short covering rather than new borrowed bets, which still left XRP up 2.67%.
XRP climbed back above $1.40 from a weekly low near $1.32 and held above its 200-day average at $1.38, so the bounce cleared a level buyers watch, which pushed XRP up 2.67% on the day.

nextPoints.text: XRP likely holds near $1.38 to $1.40 but struggles to go much higher, because FXStreet's John Isige sees bearish momentum signals and the CPI report and Fed decision coming up.

US spot SOL ETFs lost money four days in a row through 8 Oct, $19.9 million across five trading days, after a record $188 million inflow in late September, so a big buyer turned seller, which left SOL with less support and it fell about 9.6% on the week.

SOL fell about 9.6% against bitcoin's 3.1%, and record network use of 1.88 million daily active addresses did not stop holders from selling, so the network's own activity was not enough, which left SOL the weakest of the large coins.
